guard.note: builds every namespace entry through sources.entrySet().forEach, then calls base.apply(context) once: the two calls this switch wraps
puts key -> value.apply(context): the build that throws for a noise the registry lacks

asks the biome namespace's rule and, when it answers null or the namespace has none, the base rule: an entry that answers nothing is the same as no entry (3.0.1.11 keeps the last biome's rule in a field)

terrablender_stale_layer_guard.conversion: @WrapOperation of the base.apply(context) call in NamespacedSurfaceRuleSource.apply counts, per thread, the TerraBlender bases being applied; @ModifyArg (priority 900, inside terrablender_lazy_namespace_rules' consumer) of the sources.entrySet().forEach consumer: in an inner layer (a saved copy read back from level.dat; the count is above zero) every entry is passed on as a GuardedSource around the original value. Its build (at once, or at first use when the lazy switch defers it) runs the original call; the IllegalStateException HolderGetter.getOrThrow throws for a noise the registry lacks makes that layer's entry answer nothing from then on (remembered per layer object and namespace, one WARN per namespace and noise); any other exception is rethrown. The outermost layer is never wrapped. Helper bons.furious.patch.terrablender_stale.StaleLayerGuard (runtime flag staleLayerGuard). Fix: a saved layer that needs a noise no installed mod provides any more (VanillaBackport 1.2's minecraft:small_patch after a change to 1.1.7.10) crashed every new chunk of that dimension.
